title: Testing, Security, Observability & Performance
description: Make quality observable through tests, threat-driven labs, production evidence, and measurement-first performance work.

lessons.title: Testing by Risk and Boundary
lessons.why: Here’s the simple reason this matters: Good testing effort follows risk. Put the strongest test at the boundary where a failure would be expensive or where simpler tests cannot prove the behavior. In this course, we connect it directly to tests, security controls, telemetry, incidents, and performance evidence, so you can see where the idea lives in a real project instead of memorizing a definition.
objectives: Explain Testing by Risk and Boundary in terms of inputs, owner, outputs, and failure modes.
Implement Testing by Risk and Boundary incrementally and predict observable evidence before execution.
Diagnose a controlled Testing by Risk and Boundary failure from evidence.
Apply Testing by Risk and Boundary to a new TaskFlow requirement without copying the reference implementation.
prerequisites: Complete the previous lesson in Testing, Security, Observability & Performance or demonstrate equivalent skill.
Start from a healthy project/checkpoint.
mentalModel: Start with the plain-English idea. Good testing effort follows risk. Put the strongest test at the boundary where a failure would be expensive or where simpler tests cannot prove the behavior.

Now place it in TaskFlow. This lesson belongs to tests, security controls, telemetry, incidents, and performance evidence. Ask four questions while you work: what enters this boundary, who owns the decision, what dependency does it use, and what evidence proves the result?

Keep the change small. Predict what you should see before you run anything, then compare the prediction with the real terminal, browser, HTTP, database, test, container, or CI evidence. If they differ, debug the first mismatch instead of editing several places at random.

The goal is not to remember the exact snippet below. The goal is to be able to explain Testing by Risk and Boundary in your own words, rebuild the core behavior, and adapt it when the requirement changes.
